title: 'A blowout': US added 165,000 jobs in October, trouncing expectations
summary:
The US added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past economists' expectations, as the labor market showed strength despite the Federal Reserve's recent rate hikes.
September's underwhelming jobs report of 29,000 additions was also revised upward to a gain of 60,000 jobs.
Employers added jobs in a number of sectors of the economy.
Healthcare, long a strong spot for job growth, added a higher-than-average 42,000 positions.
Other job market measures released earlier this week telegraphed steady hiring — though not to the extent of Friday's report blowout number.

A jobs report on Friday showed hiring accelerated in October, providing the first major snapshot of the economy since the midterms as the stock market seesaws in response to the election results.
Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, an increase from 60,000 jobs added a month earlier, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed.
Hiring in October came in well above an average of 48,000 jobs added each month over the previous 12 months, the BLS said.

title: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates
summary:
SynopsisStronger than expected US jobs growth has revived expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike, with employers adding 165,000 jobs in October against estimates of 65,000.
The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while markets raised the probability of a quarter point hike to 85% and brought forward expectations of another increase.

title: Elizabeth Warren will take over the Senate Banking Committee next year. Expect hearings.
summary:
Democratic firebrand Elizabeth Warren, a consumer advocate known for her fierce battles over financial regulations, will take the gavel in January to become chair of the powerful Senate Banking Committee.
Earlier this year, she rallied Democrats to oppose Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's confirmation before the banking committee, stalling his eventual confirmation.
Before Republicans regained control of Congress, Democrats would have the chief executives of big banks testify before the Senate Banking and House Financial Services committees once a year.
"If people will be held under oath and there's a prospect of perjury, that will deter people from doing 'Trumpier' things," Angel said in an interview.
Angel also noted that any Trump appointee who has to be confirmed by Warren's committee will need to withstand bipartisan scrutiny and thus is more likely to be a moderate.

title: U.S. Added 165,000 Jobs In October; Entertainment Employment Rises
summary:
The U.S. added an unexpectedly robust 165,000 jobs in October, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%, while jobs in the entertainment industry also picked up.
But the unemployment rate has hovered around 4.1% to 4.3% for much of the year.
The biggest job gains were in professional and business services, healthcare and transportation and warehousing.
In movie and music production, there were 3,200 jobs added to 328,400, while broadcasting and content providers added about 200, to 327,600.
